test.//: These specs are the workspace's cross-cutting guards: they read `apps/` and `libs/` as TEXT precisely because the Nx boundaries stop any one project from importing it all. That makes them the one suite whose inputs cannot be `{projectRoot}/**/*` — this project has no dependency edges, so under the default `['default', '^production']` nothing the specs actually read was part of the cache key and every run after the first reported a stale pass. Measured: a `--trinity-text-muted: #f5f5f5` injected into `variables.scss` still returned exit 0 from the cache while `--skip-nx-cache` returned 1. Each entry below is a glob some spec really opens — the stylesheet/template/TS sweeps (`styling-idiom`, `styling-tokens`, `token-resolve`, `shorthand-overrides`, `component-styling`, `host-directives`, `scroll-behaviour`, `contrast-matrix`, `boot-splash`), the tag and vendor-boundary tables `lint-invariants` reads out of every `project.json` and out of `eslint.config.mjs`, the probe files it proves still exist, and the version tables `stack-versions` compares against what pnpm installed. The E2E module globs are deliberately broader than today's `e2e-shared-harness` reads: that guard begins with the whole module corpus before excluding shared helpers, reads `synapse/start.mjs` directly, and must stay cached when a future invariant reaches another helper.
